title: Maximal voluntary back-extension moment about L5/S1 at five lumbar flexion-extension angles (side-lying swivel table), males
subcategory: primary MVC moment vs lumbar posture

source.sample: 4 healthy tall males (chosen for MR resolution)

quantity.name: maximal voluntary isometric extension moment
quantity.definition: group mean (SD) maximal static back-extension torque about the L5/S1 disc (placed over the swivel-table centre of rotation)

protocol.summary: Subjects lying on their right side; pelvis and straight legs tightly fixed to a vertical board; back fixed to another board on a swivel table whose centre of rotation was under the L5/S1 disc; torque from a force transducer on a wire fixing the swivel table (known lever arm). Five angles between leg/pelvis board and trunk board: -45, -30, -10, +10, +20 deg (positive = lumbar extension). IAP measured simultaneously (oesophageal-gastric transducer).
how_to_simulate: Side-lying (gravity acting laterally, so no sagittal gravitational moment), pelvis and legs fixed
Set lumbar flexion-extension angle between pelvis and trunk to -45, -30, -10, +10, +20 deg (MR: -34.7±5.6 deg swivel ≈ T11-S1 angle 18.6 deg; +20 deg ≈ T11-S1 73.3 deg)
Maximal voluntary back extension against the trunk board
Compare predicted maximal extension moment about L5-S1 with mean ± SD; check the ~2.7x increase from +20 to -45 deg
protocol.notes: Signs of angles reconstructed from text ('positive angular direction coincides with lumbar back extension'; minus signs lost in PDF text layer, confirmed on Fig 2 axis labels). The IAP-generated torque in Fig 2 is a model output (not stored). Measured IAP 12-19 kPa at maximal effort (Fig 3) not stored here.

data.from: text (Fig 8 caption: 109.2±17.8 Nm at the most extended position = swivel +20 deg); Fig 2 digitised 108.9±15.9

extraction.check_notes: Bars digitised by pixel analysis (tick calibration 0-350 Nm). Cross-check: -45/+20 ratio 297.6/109.2 = 2.72 vs text '2.7 times'; +20 deg bar 108.9±15.9 vs caption 109.2±17.8 (caption used).
